patternsObserved.heroes: Top performers use full-bleed video or cinematic carousels with a persistent reserve CTA; logo-first static heroes (Don Angie, Dante) read flat by comparison
patternsObserved.palettes: Fine-dining consensus = dark base + one metallic accent (COTE black/gold, Carbone burgundy/gold); tapas brands go warm red/white; nobody owns navy+azulejo blue - open lane for Buena Vista
patternsObserved.booking: Resy dominates NYC prestige tier (Cosme, Carbone, COTE, DCP, Llama Inn); multi-location brands route through location cards or an embedded location-picker form (Jaleo, Dante, COTE)
patternsObserved.platforms: BentoBox powers most (Jaleo, Tatiana, Llama Inn); differentiation comes from art direction, not tech
patternsObserved.content: Chef narrative, press walls, prix-fixe 'experience' tiers, and material/interior storytelling are the recurring premium signals
patternsObserved.motion: Motion is used sparingly and purposefully even at the top tier - COTE is the ceiling (floating SVGs, autoplay video, scroll transitions), everyone else stays subtle

designRecommendations.heroDirection: Full-bleed cinematic video hero, 8-12s seamless loop: slow dolly across the paella pan mid-flame -> saffron steam close-up -> glassware and candlelight in the Hell's Kitchen dining room. Grade it dark and warm over a deep navy #1E3A5F base wash. Overlay: azulejo-tile-pattern gold monogram, 'Spain Meets Latin America' in large display serif, two CTAs ('Reserve a Table' gold solid, 'View Menus' ghost outline) plus a subtle location switcher (Hell's Kitchen | East Village). Fallback: graded still with slow Ken Burns for reduced-motion/slow connections. Kill the Popmenu 'Load More Content' pattern entirely - the whole story loads on scroll.

paletteGuidance.strategy: Own the azulejo lane no NYC competitor occupies: navy-and-gold cinematic dark mode with cream editorial breaks
paletteGuidance.base: #1E3A5F azulejo navy - primary background for hero, menus, footer (replaces the current dark gray)
paletteGuidance.surface: #F7F2E9 cream - alternating light sections (story, press, private events) for rhythm and readability
paletteGuidance.accent: #C9995C gold - the ONLY CTA/button/link-hover color; retire the Popmenu green #0A7D57 completely
paletteGuidance.supporting: #2E5A8F mid blue for hover states, menu-tab actives, and map pins; #A8C4E5 sky blue only in azulejo tile pattern dividers and illustrated flourishes, never for text
paletteGuidance.rules: Never place gold text on cream at small sizes (contrast); body text is cream-on-navy or near-black #1A1A18 on cream; tile patterns at 6-10% opacity as section-break textures, full-strength only in the logo and dividers

primary.display: Fraunces (Google Fonts) - high-contrast 'wonky' serif with optical sizing; feels hand-set Iberian-editorial, dramatically better than the current Libre Baskerville; use 72-120px hero, soft optical size, weights 300-600
primary.body: Figtree (Google Fonts) - warm geometric sans, excellent at 15-17px; use for menu items, hours, addresses, buttons (letterspaced uppercase 12-13px for CTAs/labels)

alternate.display: Marcellus - single-weight Trajan-like serif, Spanish-classical, ultra-elegant if Fraunces reads too playful
alternate.body: Jost - clean grotesque, pairs cleanly with Marcellus

typographyPairing.menuNumerals: Use Fraunces tabular/oldstyle figures for prices so the menu pages feel typeset, not templated

sectionOrder: 1. Hero - cinematic video, tagline, Reserve + Menus CTAs, location switcher, sticky nav appears on scroll with persistent gold Reserve button
2. Story strip - 'Spain Meets Latin America' two-line manifesto on cream, azulejo divider, founded-2018 + Christian Nunez one-liner (link to full story)
3. Signature dishes - horizontal scroll-driven showcase: Paella (flagship, largest card), Ceviche Limeno $21, Salmon Barceloneta $27, BV Cocktails; each with reserve micro-CTA
4. Menus - tabbed navy section: Lunch / Dinner / Brunch / Pre-Fixe / Drinks / Wine / Zero-Proof / Kids; PDF-free, HTML menus with Fraunces price typography

5. Two Locations - split panel cards (COTE location-card pattern): Hell's Kitchen (536 9th Ave, (212) 388-5040) vs East Village (88 2nd Ave, (929) 220-0547), each with hours (incl. Fri-Sat late-night difference), map, tap-to-call, and its own Reserve button
6. The Bar - BV Cocktails + zero-proof program, moody cocktail photography on navy
7. Private events & Pre-Fixe experiences - cream section, inquiry form (Boqueria 'experience tier' framing)
8. Owner story - Christian Nunez portrait + heritage narrative (Tatiana treatment)
9. Press + social proof - awards/quotes as design elements (Dante pattern) + Instagram feed strip (@buenavistany)
10. Footer - navy: newsletter capture, both locations' hours/phones, socials (IG/FB/TikTok/YouTube), reserve links
motionInteraction: Azulejo tile mosaic 'assembles' as the hero loads (staggered 40ms tile fade-ins) - the signature brand moment, reused subtly on section dividers
Scroll-triggered reveals: 24px translate-up + fade, 350ms ease-out, staggered 80ms per child; never bounce easing
Signature-dish showcase: horizontal scroll-jacking-free sticky panel with progress dots (works as vertical stack on mobile)
Ken Burns 1.03x slow zoom on all still photography; parallax at max 8% on tile-texture backgrounds
Sticky reserve button: appears after hero, gold pill, docks bottom-right on mobile as a thumb-reachable FAB
Menu tabs crossfade 200ms; prices count no animation (keep menus calm)
prefers-reduced-motion: disable video autoplay, parallax, and tile assembly; everything must read perfectly static

bookingCtaStrategy.primary: Persistent gold 'Reserve a Table' in sticky nav -> location-picker modal (two cards with next-available context) -> deep link into their reservation platform per location (verify current Popmenu/OpenTable/Resy setup during build; recommend migrating to Resy or OpenTable direct deep links with pre-filled party/date params like Cosme)
bookingCtaStrategy.secondary: Per-location Reserve buttons on location cards and after the menus section; reserve micro-CTAs on signature dish cards
bookingCtaStrategy.tertiary: Tap-to-call phone buttons per location on mobile; 'Order Online' as a quieter text link (not competing with Reserve); private-events inquiry form for groups 8+
bookingCtaStrategy.rules: One gold CTA per viewport max; never open reservations in a hijacking overlay on mobile - full-screen sheet instead; repeat Reserve at hero, post-menus, each location card, and footer

photographyArtDirection.grade: Dark moody editorial: navy-teal shadows, warm gold highlights - grade every asset to the brand palette so navy #1E3A5F and gold #C9995C exist inside the photos themselves
photographyArtDirection.heroVideo: Flame, steam, and pour moments: paella socarrat sizzle, saffron broth pour, cocktail garnish drop; 24fps look, shallow depth, slight slow-motion (60fps conformed)
photographyArtDirection.food: Overhead hero shot of the full paella pan as the flagship image; 3/4 low-angle plates lit by single warm key light mimicking candlelight; azulejo tiles and cream linens as surface props to embed brand into every frame
photographyArtDirection.space: Dusk interiors with practical lamps, bar bottle-wall glow, both locations shot in the same grade for brand cohesion
photographyArtDirection.people: Christian Nunez environmental portrait in the dining room; hands-only service moments (carving, pouring) over posed staff shots
photographyArtDirection.formats: Shoot 16:9 video + 4:5 and 1:1 stills in the same sessions for site/Instagram/TikTok reuse; one photographer for the whole library (Don Angie lesson)

designRecommendations.competitiveOpening: No NYC Latin/Spanish competitor owns a navy-blue azulejo identity - Jaleo and Boqueria both run warm red/festive palettes. Pairing COTE's dark-cinematic system with Buena Vista's existing tile brand creates a category-of-one look: 'Iberian jewel-box' rather than 'tapas-party', matching the $$$ positioning.
